summary: Seven of nine slots locked. Stafford's game is the one that hurts — 4.1 showing against a 16.6 projection with Lawrence on your bench. Flex is the only live call and I am staying with Tuten over Lloyd.

items.headline: Jonathan Taylor — locked in
items.evidence: RB4, clean bell cow, no committee. Baltimore at home.

items.headline: Saquon Barkley — locked in
items.evidence: RB5 against Washington. Bigsby's camp split has not shown up in the projection and should not change the start.

items.headline: Rashee Rice — locked in
items.evidence: WR13, camp target leader, no further suspension. Sunday night.

items.headline: Colston Loveland — locked in
items.evidence: TE2 overall. Odunze is questionable with a calf, which only concentrates the targets further.

items.headline: Jaguars D/ST — locked in
items.evidence: Consensus number one defence this week.

items.headline: Stafford is showing 4.1 against a 16.6 projection
items.evidence: His actual has not moved in ten hours, so the number is settled rather than live.
items.body: Lawrence projected 16.0 at rank 8 on your bench. Start Lawrence from week 2 unless a matchup says otherwise — and note his bye is week 7, the same week Tuten, the Jaguars defence and Little are all out.

items.headline: Tuten holds the flex over Lloyd
items.evidence: Lloyd projects higher at 12.8 but Stenavich called it committee across three backs, and Green Bay is on the road against a Minnesota front that gave up the fourth-lowest stuff rate. Jacksonville is a 7.5-point home favourite against the worst offensive line in football, which is the game script a running back wants.
items.body: Closer than it was this morning. If Lloyd takes the first two series outright this becomes a week-2 problem worth revisiting.
